items.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: the music that appealed to me most then was the pianists Fats Waller and Teddy Wilson... Those were my first influences.

ctx.x: Tell us about some of your influences, some of your keyboard influences.

Well at the beginning you know since it happened when I was eleven, twelve years old taking those piano lessons, the music that appealed to me most then was the pianists Fats Waller and Teddy Wilson. Really different kinds of pianists but I loved them both. They were both great. Particularly Teddy. I even tried to imitate him, like get his records and try to play like him you know. And many years passed and I was able to meet him and we even traveled together on two different trips — one over in Russia for six…
Who was your favorite bebop artist on keyboard?
